properties.name: Transbay Terminal loop, San Francisco
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (23 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The loop as the 1950 sheet draws it ("KEY SYSTEM"): from the approach, north along the west side to the terminal's west end, through the six-track station facing Mission Street, around the east end and back south. Trains ran counter-clockwise, arriving at the station's east end.

sources.note: "the tracks form a large loop with a six-track, double-end station on the north side of the loop. This station faces Mission street … All trains normally run counter-clockwise in this loop" (p. 150).
"an elevated concrete and steel structure that looped some two-thirds of a mile" (p. 31); "The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958" (p. 215).

properties.name: San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, lower deck
properties.geometry_method: Joined to bbr-sf-loop at its start; then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco North 1:24,000 (1950) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 2 m)); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (8 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From Rincon Hill across the bridge's lower deck, through the Yerba Buena Island tunnel, to where the tracks left the bridge on its south side at the Oakland end. The 1946-50 sheets draw the bridge, not the tracks on it; the tracks were on the south half of the lower deck.

sources.note: "the lower deck has three lanes for trucks and buses, and two tracks equipped for electrical propulsion" (p. 148); "Train service over the bridge was placed in operation on Jan. 15" (p. 154).
The trains used "the southern half of the lower deck" (p. 231); "The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958" (p. 215).

properties.name: East Bay approach and yards
properties.geometry_method: Joined to bbr-bridge at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (6 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along the south side of the bridge approach ("KEY SYSTEM" on the 1949 sheet) past the toll plaza to the East Bay yards, where the Key System's and the Interurban's tracks divided.

sources.note: The old Key System layout on the mole was "entirely rebuilt … to provide connections from the bridge tracks to inbound and outbound tracks of both roads, without crossings at grade, but also to provide a yard for each road" (p. 150).
The bridge "touched down on what had been a train yard island, or 'mole'" (p. 29).
"the service yards and facilities on the eastern approach to the bridge, including the overhead wye at 26th Street in Oakland".

properties.name: Interurban lead to 26th Street
properties.geometry_method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (7 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). The Interurban's double-track lead from the bridge yards east to the Y at 26th Street, where it met the old Southern Pacific main line.

sources.note: "The Interurban Electric Railway trains used a double-tracked lead from the Bridge Yards to a Y-shaped viaduct near the foot of 26th Street … the point of divergence was named 26th Street Junction."
Track "west of the overhead wye is owned by the State of California … the remainder east of the wye is owned by Southern Pacific Company … and leased to Interurban".
